messages:
marta: thinking out loud — we should try an 'economy-first' fanout for low-SKU customers during peak hours. route to the cheaper float16/q4 variants unless latency SLOs are violated.
arnav: +1 for cost control but we need hard guards: token-budget per-request and a per-customer daily ceiling. otherwise customers silently lose quality.
jia: how do we define 'low-SKU'? by committed monthly spend or by runtime quota?
marta: committed spend tier by default, but allow overrides in console per project. default mapping: free/dev => economy, standard => balanced, pro/enterprise => performance.
samir: what about region concerns? cheaper variant may not be available in some zones. fallback order should prefer same-region cheaper model, then cross-region, then escalate to a performance variant if compatibility mismatch.
marta: exactly. want a deterministic policy: 1) same-region cheapest compatible; 2) same-region next-compatible; 3) cross-region cheapest within latency budget; 4) performance fallback only if above fail.
arnav: and add token-cost accounting: prefer cheaper models only when estimated token-cost delta > X (e.g., >10% savings) OR when customer's per-day spend is nearing the ceiling. avoids micro-switching for trivial differences.
opsbot: deploy/checklist created: #2345 Economy fanout feature flag + metrics.
jia: console UX ask: customers must be able to opt out of economy routing at project level and set a max-per-token budget. add a toggle and a numeric cap.
marta: UI note: show an estimated cost-savings badge and an estimated quality delta (from evals) next to the toggle. helps PMs decide.
samir: from infra side, we need a fast decision path — cannot call cost estimator synchronously for every token. precompute per-model per-sequence-length unit-cost table and cache it per-region. config example: 
```
policy: economy_fanout_v1
matchers:
  - customer_tier: free, dev
  - peak_window: 18:00-22:00
rules:
  - try: model: redwood-econ-q4f
    region_preference: local
    max_latency_ms: 350
  - try: model: redwood-econ-q4f-cross
    region_preference: cross
    max_latency_ms: 450
  - fallback: model: redwood-std-16b
    note: preserve-quality
cost_threshold_pct: 10
token_budget_guard: true
```
arnav: love the config. add 'graceful-degrade' flag so that if a cheaper model returns hallucinations or safety flags we auto-roll to the next rule immediately for the session.
marta: telemetry plan: emit route_decision for every request (rule_id, chosen_model, est_cost, actual_tokens, latency_ms) and aggregate: cost_saved_by_tier, failed_fallbacks, cross_region_ratio.
jia: and expose a per-project chart in console: weekly token spend vs. cost-saved-by-economy-routing + number of quality regressions flagged by eval hooks.
samir: rollout plan: feature-flag per-org. start with alpha orgs in eu-west and us-east; run canaries with 1% traffic, then 10%, then 50%. watch these metrics: latency_p95, model_reject_rate, quality_regression_rate (from eval syndrome).
arnav: alerting: when quality_regression_rate > 0.5% for 24h or cost_saved < 1% at 50% rollout -> automatic rollback.
marta: edge-case: token budgeting + streaming. if we switch mid-stream to a cheaper variant, the KV cache won't match. plan: do per-session binding — decision at session start for chat sessions; allow per-request switching for stateless generation.
jia: question: billing implications — customers on pay-as-you-go expect lower-cost models to reduce invoice. do we show 'estimated effective price per token' in invoices?
arnav: yes. show line-items: base_token_cost, economy_discount_applied. need accounting proof for audits.
samir: ops note: ensure billing/usage pipeline gets 'chosen_model' tag for each request. otherwise we can't attribute cost.
opsbot: action created: #2350 Add chosen_model tag to usage events (owner: eng-infra).
marta: next steps: write a short RFC for policy DSL, add UI mockups for opt-out and budget cap, and schedule canary with eng-sre. I'll spin up the RFC draft tomorrow.
arnav: i'll handle the telemetry schema. jia can you mock the console copy and visuals?
jia: on it.
samir: i'll scope infra changes and estimate perf cost for cross-region routing.
marta: thanks — let's sync on Friday for runbook and SLA notes. :thumbsup:
